first_impression.reaction: Mykonos. I'll admit I think of it as a party island, so I opened this a bit wary. But the opening is calm and sensible: five parts of the island, and the choice depends on guest numbers, the ceremony and how people get around. No gushing. I'll read it properly.

journey.quote: Greek summers bring frequent heatwaves and a wildfire season from June to September, so plan shade, a later ceremony and a covered fallback for a summer date.
journey.reaction: Good, the heat and the fires are up front. That's the first thing I worry about with Mum.

journey.section: Mykonos wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity | Exclusive use |
journey.reaction: Manageable on the iPad, though I had to slide it across. So many boxes say 'Not published' that I wonder what the table is telling me. I'll go through it with my husband on the computer.

journey.section: How to compare Mykonos venues like for like
journey.quote: Add three questions to every list: is there a step-free route between rooms, ceremony and reception; what is the plan on a windy afternoon; and what time must the music stop?
journey.reaction: Finally. Step-free route is exactly what I'd ask, and I didn't have to feel like the fussy one for asking. My mother and her walking frame are the first thing I think of.

journey.section: How to compare Mykonos venues like for like
journey.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from curfew to minimum nights, your Wedded Advisor confirms in writing with the venue before you commit, so [talk to a Wedded Advisor about your shortlist]
journey.reaction: In writing, before we commit, and a named role who does the checking. That's someone accountable. Said once, clearly, which I prefer.

journey.section: Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: The hotel's rule is that both bride and groom must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.
journey.reaction: Glad that's spelled out. That's precisely the sort of thing a couple falls in love with and then finds out too late.

journey.section: Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: A whitewashed chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary, "perched on a hill looking out over Ayios Yiannis Beach".
journey.reaction: Pretty, but 'perched on a hill' means steps to me. Neither this chapel nor any other says whether Mum could get up there.

journey.section: Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: With two indoor reception spaces, Saint John also has a ready answer for an evening when the wind picks up.
journey.reaction: Sensible. I like when the article thinks about what goes wrong, not just the sunset.

journey.quote: - **Not published:** ceremony types, exclusive use, curfew.
journey.reaction: By the fifth or sixth venue the 'Not published' lines all blur together. I know it's honest, but I started skimming them.

journey.section: ZeNIT Events Center, above Paradise beach
journey.quote: The venue's own services include a physician and medical room during events, security with CCTV, and guest transfers that ZeNIT runs itself for up to 16 guests, with larger groups handled through its partners and transfers by sea also offered.
journey.reaction: Now that's the line I'd read out to my husband. A doctor on site and transfers they run themselves. I wish every venue told me that much.

journey.section: Getting to Mykonos for your wedding
journey.quote: From the airport, a bus runs to Mykonos Town (Chora) and other destinations from a stop in front of the terminal in the Arrivals area, with tickets bought from the driver.
journey.reaction: Useful for the young cousins, but I'm not putting an 88-year-old on a bus with her luggage after two days of flying. I'd want to know who organises a proper transfer.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/europe/greece) says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion and heat stroke, and that many major tourist sites have little shade.
journey.reaction: Government advice, dated. I trust that. Nothing about travel or medical insurance though, which is the first thing I'd sort for Mum.

journey.quote: Ask the destination's embassy or consulate:
journey.reaction: Nicely broken into a short list, easy to follow. I still don't know who actually does the paperwork in the end: the couple, the venue or the Advisor.

journey.section: Shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, the fee in writing. That's the paragraph my husband needs to see. I'd still want a phone call before a cent changes hands.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues have step-free or level access from rooms to the chapel or terrace, for a guest with a walking frame? The article tells me to ask but no venue answers.
Who arranges private airport transfers for older guests, other than the bus or taxi queue?
What travel or medical insurance should older guests carry for a summer wedding in Greece?
Who prepares and lodges the legal paperwork, such as the CNI: the couple, the venue or the Wedded Advisor?
Who reads a venue contract in Greek and in euros, and is the venue deposit protected?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Mykonos time?
Is the first step a phone call with the Wedded Advisor, before anything is booked or paid?
would_share_with: My husband, with the closing section (fee in writing, AUD) and the ZeNIT 'On the day' line about a physician and transfers
My daughter, with the Mykonos Grand Orthodox rule and the 'three questions to every list' paragraph
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the heat, wildfire and swimming advice

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: A named person, Australian time, AUD and the fee in writing tick most of my boxes. I'd click if it said plainly that a real person rings me first, before anything is booked, and that they'll check which venues my mother can actually get around.

top_3_changes: Add 'step-free access' to the per-venue 'Not published' lines (or to the list the Wedded Advisor confirms in writing), and flag the hilltop chapels (Mykonos Grand) and the hilltop ZeNIT for guests with limited mobility.
In 'Getting to Mykonos' and 'When to marry', add a line on organised transfers for older guests and on travel and medical insurance for a summer date.
Say in one plain sentence who handles the legal paperwork in practice, and trim the repeated per-venue 'Not published' bullet so it doesn't duplicate the lines just above it.

open_questions.question: This draft improves on Corfu for this persona: it raises step-free routes and ZeNIT publishes a physician and transfers. The gaps left are venue-level accessibility (no venue answers the step-free question), insurance, and organised transfers. Treat as should-fix? Deposit, contract language and on-the-day contact are deferred business details.

Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
